insight: Net sales grew from 2020 to 2025 at 16.6% a year, but units grew only 5.0% a year; on average 11.3 percentage points of annual growth came from higher prices and mix, 5.0 from volume.
recommendation: Track volume growth as a separate KPI; price-led growth is not sustainable indefinitely.

insight: After controlling for product, year and season, the estimated price elasticity of demand is +0.09 (95% CI -0.28 to +0.46), i.e. not significantly different from zero. Discounts show no relationship with order size (Spearman rho = 0.001).
recommendation: Review the discount budget (BDT 7.7 million over the period): discounts do not appear to buy volume.

insight: December is the peak month (index 125, average month = 100) and February the weakest (86). The seasonal effect is statistically strong (Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.001).
recommendation: Build stock and distributor capacity from October; schedule promotions and maintenance in February.

insight: Muffin is the largest category (22.4% of sales); the top 10 of 52 products deliver 38.5% of revenue and 27 products form the 'A' class (80% of sales).
recommendation: Protect availability of A-class products first; review C-class products for rationalisation or repositioning.

insight: Clustering finds 5 product segments; 'Premium & gift packs' grows fastest (+7.8% units a year, 33.3% of sales).
recommendation: Prioritise shelf space and marketing for 'Premium & gift packs'.

insight: Dhaka alone generates 43.9% of sales and Dhaka plus Chattogram 58.3%. General Trade is the largest channel (45.6%), while E-commerce is 5.9%.
recommendation: Reduce concentration risk by developing secondary cities and scaling E-commerce, which grows from a small base.

insight: The 'Emerging high-growth cells' segment (19 region-channel-customer cells, mainly Cumilla, Khulna, Mymensingh) is growing at +33.2% a year, the fastest of the 4 market segments.
recommendation: Allocate field-sales and digital-marketing effort to these emerging cells.

insight: Whether an order will be large (>= 10 units) is moderately predictable (best ROC-AUC 0.712, Logistic Regression); channel is by far the strongest driver: 48% of distributor orders are large versus 8% online.
recommendation: Use the large-order score for delivery-vehicle and stock allocation, mainly at channel level.

insight: The Support Vector Regression model forecasts next month's product demand with 11.1% weighted error, 24% lower RMSE than the seasonal-naive rule. Net sales for 2026-10 to 2027-09 are forecast at BDT 76.3 million (+12.1% on the previous 12 months; 80% range BDT 72.7 million - BDT 79.9 million).
recommendation: Use the product-level forecast for the monthly production plan and the interval for safety stock.

insight: 28 of 2,465 trading days were flagged as unusual. In a controlled test, rules plus Isolation Forest caught 91% of 1,000 planted data errors.
recommendation: Run the anomaly screen daily and investigate flagged days and orders before month-end reporting.
